en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Rochelle Park (Garfield volume), Bergen County, New Jersey, 1917, Sheet 63, part 1 (upper part: Rochelle Avenue, Oak Avenue, Central Avenue)
Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Rochelle Park (Garfield volume), Bergen County, New Jersey, 1917, Sheet 63, part 2 (lower part: Terrace Avenue to Thiem Avenue, Brooks Avenue, Rochelle Avenue)

sheet-63-1.description: The upper part of sheet 63 of the 1917 Garfield volume shows the centre of Rochelle Park, Bergen County, at 100 feet to an inch, drawn with north to the right. Rochelle Avenue runs along the top of the part. Below it, at the left, Park Way leads away from Rochelle Avenue with the short streets Elm and Pine, both marked as arbitrary names, and a few blocks of house lots. The railroad crosses Rochelle Avenue left of centre; beside it are the passenger station, a freight house and the D.S. MacMullen coal elevator with its sheds, wagon shed and lath pile. Along Rochelle Avenue east of the railroad stand a row of one and two storey stores, a post office, a pool and bowling hall and storage buildings. Oak and Central Avenue leave Rochelle Avenue at an angle and run toward the lower left, crossing William, Colling Avenue and Susquehanna Avenue, which are laid out in long narrow lots with scattered frame dwellings. A fire department hall stands on William. The Red Rock Inn is at the upper right corner. Much of the area between Oak and Central Avenue (blocks 6 and 7) is still undivided or lightly built. The title block with the town's population, fire department and water notes sits at the top left and is left out of the mask. The heavy line along the bottom divides this part from the lower part of the sheet, which is drawn at a different angle.
notes: Printed sheet 63 of the Garfield volume; Rochelle Park lies about 2.5 miles northeast of Garfield.
Modern names: Park Way is Parkway; Oak is Oak Street; William is William Street; Elm (arbitrary) matches St Ann Place, and Pine (arbitrary) the southward turn of Parkway.
Title block: population 900, volunteer fire company of 75 members, streets of gravel.

Rochelle Park, printed sheet 63 of the Garfield volume, 1917, 100 ft to an inch, three parts divided by heavy lines. Part 1 (upper): Rochelle Av along the top with Park Way, Elm and Pine (both marked Arbitrary), the railroad with passenger station and D.S. MacMullen coal elevator, Oak, Central Av, William, Colling Av and Susquehanna Av; north is to the right. Part 2 (lower): Terrace Av, Forest Pl, Chestnut Av, Thiem Av and Brooks Av above Rochelle Av, with Chestnut Av, Marinus, Oldis, Catharine and Peek below it; drawn about 33 degrees from part 1. Part 3 (inset, right): Saddle River Road along the Saddle River, no cross street; not placed. Title and notes block and the scale bar are cut out of the masks.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Saddle River Road along the Saddle River (blocks 26 and 27) (no street junction; only Saddle River Road and the river are drawn, with distance notes (650 ft to the railroad freight house, 900 ft to the fire house); needs a hand-placed point on Saddle River Road (for example from the 650 ft distance to the railroad crossing) plus north_deg; low confidence).

sheet-63-2.description: The lower part of sheet 63 of the 1917 Garfield volume covers the northern side of Rochelle Park at 100 feet to an inch, drawn about a third of a right angle from the upper part, with north toward the upper right. Rochelle Avenue runs across the bottom of the part. North of it, Terrace Avenue, Forest Place, Chestnut Avenue and Thiem Avenue run up the sheet, joined by Brooks Avenue; the blocks between them (12 to 18) are large and only partly built, with frame dwellings mostly along Terrace and Thiem Avenues. Sacred Heart Catholic Church stands on Terrace Avenue with a 5,000 gallon tank beside it. South of Rochelle Avenue a row of blocks (20 to 25) is cut by Chestnut Avenue, Marinus, Oldis, Catharine and Peek, mostly vacant lots at the bottom edge of the sheet. Public School No. 5 is at the lower right corner. The large block 19 at the right is empty apart from the compass rose. A fire alarm box stands at Rochelle Avenue and Terrace Avenue, where Rochelle Avenue bends toward the lower left. The heavy line along the top divides this part from the upper part, and the Saddle River Road inset at the right (part 3) and the scale bar are left out of the mask.
notes: Modern names: Chestnut Avenue north of Rochelle Avenue is Chestnut Street; Thiem Avenue is Theim Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Marinus is Marinus Street; Oldis is Oldis Street; Catharine is Catherine Street; Peek is Peek Street.
The modern Chestnut Avenue / Chestnut Street / Rochelle Avenue node lies about 4.5 m from the drawn junction and is left out of the fit.
Brooks Avenue is not drawn through to Terrace Avenue.
